transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, um… I’m probably not explaining it the best way, but people at work have been having trouble following me lately. Like when I’m trying to go over inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, I start out talking about one thing and then somehow I’m onto the trucks, or Thursday, or the church grill, or my boss’s tone, and I can see people looking at me like they’re lost.

I don’t mean to be confusing. I’m trying to answer correctly, you know? It’s just… my words kind of jump around, and it’s been enough that I thought I should come in and ask about it.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed your mood feeling unusually high, euphoric, or irritable, along with having much more energy than usual?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I wouldn’t say “euphoric” or anything like that. Maybe I get a little tense if I’m not explaining myself well, but not like I’m full of energy or on top of the world. I’ve been trying to keep things pretty normal, if that makes sense.
Have you been using any alcohol, marijuana, or other recreational drugs recently, or taking any new medications or supplements?

Um… no, not really. I mean, I might have a drink now and then, like socially, but nothing new or heavy. I don’t use marijuana or other drugs. And I can’t think of any new medications or supplements I’ve started. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you had any recent head injuries, seizures, or new neurological symptoms like numbness, weakness, or severe headaches, or been diagnosed with any new medical illness recently?

No, I don’t think so. I haven’t hit my head or had anything like a seizure that I know of. No numbness or weakness… and headaches, not anything severe. I haven’t been told I have some new medical illness recently either. I mean, as far as I understand it, nothing like that has happened.
How long have you been noticing this pattern of your thoughts and speech jumping around like this—has it been going on for a few days, a few weeks, or longer than a month?

I guess… longer than a month, yeah. I didn’t want to make it sound too dramatic, because I can still do things, but people at work have noticed the way I explain things getting kind of jumbled, and sometimes I sort of stop oddly on the sales floor. That’s probably been going on about six months now, if I’m being honest. Is that the kind of timeframe you mean?

Over these past six months, has this jumbled, tangential way of speaking been present continuously the whole time, or has it come and gone with periods where your speech was completely back to normal?

It’s… it’s been around most of that time, I think. I don’t know that every single conversation is like that, so I don’t want to overstate it, but the jumbled explanations and those odd pauses at work have been noticeable for about six months now. I can have better moments, sure, but I wouldn’t say it completely went back to normal for a long stretch. Does that answer it okay?
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear, or seen things that others didn't see?

I don’t think so… not in the sense of, like, hearing a voice talking to me when nobody’s there, or seeing people or things that other people can’t see. Sometimes I might mishear something at work if it’s noisy, but I think that’s pretty normal. I haven’t noticed anything like what you’re asking, I don’t believe. Is that okay?

Have you had any strong beliefs recently that others might see as unusual or that they didn't agree with—like feeling that people are watching you, plotting against you, or trying to send you special messages?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I can get a little uncomfortable if I feel like people are noticing me at work, but I wouldn’t say I believe they’re watching me or plotting against me or anything like that. And I haven’t felt like messages were meant specially for me. I don’t think that’s been happening. Is that what you mean?

Has this trouble with your speech and thinking affected your ability to do your job or keep up with your usual responsibilities—have you made mistakes, been written up, or fallen behind because of it?

Yeah… I mean, I’ve still been getting things done, mostly, but it has affected work. My boss doesn’t really trust me to run the busy weekend shifts anymore, which is… hard to admit. And after my last performance review, he said if things don’t improve I could be suspended.

At home it’s been a little difficult too. My wife has had to cover some commitments I used to handle, because I guess people were getting uncomfortable or confused when I was trying to explain things. I’m not proud of that. I hope that’s the kind of thing you’re asking.
Have you noticed any new problems with your memory, like forgetting recent conversations, appointments, or having trouble finding the right words when you're speaking?

I don’t think I’ve had new memory problems, no. I mean, I forget little things here and there like anyone, but not whole conversations or appointments that I know of. Sometimes I pause when I’m talking, but I wouldn’t say I can’t find the words exactly… it’s more just trying to explain myself clearly, I guess. Does that answer it okay?

Over these past six months, have you noticed yourself pulling away from friends or family, losing interest in things you used to enjoy, or feeling like your emotions are more flat or muted than before?

I’m not sure I’d say that’s happened, no. I mean, I’ve maybe been a little quieter or kept to myself when I’m tired, but I still care about my family and I still try to do the normal things.

I don’t think my emotions feel flat, exactly. Maybe my wife would notice something I don’t, but from my side I wouldn’t describe it that way. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you hold any unusual beliefs about having special powers, being able to predict events, or that certain rituals or superstitions can influence what happens to you?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I might have little routines like anybody—checking something twice, or feeling better if I do things in a certain order—but I don’t believe I have special powers or can predict the future or anything like that.

I hope that’s clear. I’m not trying to dodge it, I just don’t think that’s been part of what’s going on.

Have people noticed you doing anything unusual with your body or behavior lately—like odd, repetitive movements, unpredictable agitation, or times when you seem to freeze up or become unusually still?

Maybe a little, yeah… nothing dramatic, I don’t think. At work sometimes I’ll find myself pacing the same aisle more than I need to, or straightening the same row of batteries over and over like I’m trying to make it perfect.

And there have been a few times where I’m standing there with the schedule clipboard in my hand, and the associates are waiting for me to tell them what to do, and I just sort of… pause too long. I wouldn’t say I freeze exactly, but I can see how it might look odd. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
When you 'pause too long' with the clipboard, how long does that stillness typically last—just a few seconds, or sometimes a minute or more where you're not moving or responding at all?

Usually it’s just a few seconds, I think… or that’s how it feels to me. I’m not just standing there for minutes not responding, at least I don’t believe so.

It’s more like I’ve got the schedule clipboard in my hand, the associates are waiting, and I sort of lose the next step for a moment. Then I catch myself and say something. I realize it may look strange, but I wouldn’t want to make it sound more serious than it is. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Have you noticed a decrease in your motivation to start or follow through with everyday tasks—like getting ready for work, doing chores, or planning things you used to do without much thought?

I’m not sure I’d call it a decrease, exactly. I still get myself to work and do the things I’m supposed to do.

Maybe some days it takes me a little longer to get going, or I put off chores longer than I should, but… I don’t know, that could just be being tired or getting older. I haven’t really thought of it as losing motivation.

Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
Have you or your wife noticed any changes in your personal hygiene or grooming—like forgetting to shower, dressing unusually, or neglecting other daily self-care tasks—over these past six months?

I don’t think so, no. My wife hasn’t really said anything like that to me, at least not that I can remember.

I still shower and get dressed for work. Maybe I’m not as particular as I used to be some mornings, but nothing like forgetting for days or wearing something really strange. If anything, I try to keep myself looking normal, especially at work.

Does that sound like the kind of thing you mean?
Would you say this jumbled, tangential way of talking happens in most of your conversations now, or only in certain situations like when you're under pressure at work?

I’d say it’s more noticeable when I’m under pressure, especially at work. Like when I’m trying to explain the inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, I’ll start on one thing and then my words kind of jump around—trucks, then Thursday, then something about the church grill, then maybe my boss’s tone—and I can tell people are looking at me like they’re not following.

I don’t think it’s every conversation, though. At least I hope not. With normal talk at home it’s not as bad, I don’t think. It’s just when I’m trying to explain something important and people are waiting on me, it gets jumbled. Does that make sense?

Yeah… I think that’s basically what brought me in, or part of it anyway. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but when I’m trying to explain things like the inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, my words start jumping around.

Like I’ll mean to talk about the trucks, and then I’m on Thursday, and then somehow I mention the church grill or my boss’s tone, and I can see people looking at me like they can’t follow. I’m trying to be clear, I really am. It just doesn’t always come out in the right order.

Outside of work, have you or your wife noticed you doing things that seem oddly disorganized or out of place—like starting a task and then doing something completely unrelated, or behaving in ways that don't fit the situation?

Outside of work… I’m not sure my wife would say it’s a big problem. I don’t think I’m doing anything really strange around the house, at least not that I notice.

At work, though—well, I guess that’s not exactly what you asked, but it’s where I notice it most. Sometimes on the sales floor I’ll catch myself pacing the same aisle, straightening the same row of batteries over and over, like I’ve already fixed it but I keep doing it. Or I’ll just be standing there with the schedule clipboard in my hand while the associates are waiting for me to tell them what to do, and I sort of… stall out.

I don’t mean to. I know what I’m supposed to be doing. It just gets kind of stuck for a minute. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?

Yeah… yes, I think so. I mean, not like I’m trying to be odd or anything. It’s more at work that I notice it.

Sometimes I’ll be on the sales floor and I’ll catch myself pacing the same aisle, or straightening the same row of batteries again and again, even though they’re already straight. Or I’ll be holding the schedule clipboard and the associates are kind of waiting for me to tell them what to do, and I just… stand there for a bit.

It’s embarrassing to say. I don’t think it happens all the time, but it does happen. Is that the sort of thing you mean?

I don’t mean to be confusing. I’m trying to answer correctly, you know? It’s just… my words kind of jump around, and it’s been enough that I thought I should come in and ask about it.
